A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SoLoPO study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v2 reports original SoLoPO training and benchmark results, including ablations, efficiency measurements, and experiments with larger models in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and additionally reports LongPO comparisons and a reward-alignment bound sensitivity experiment.

M1.justification: Appendix I.8 introduces an experimental alignment-loss variant using s_l(x)=|x|+sin(x)+1 instead of the existing s_t(x)=|x|. This is a limited ablation variant; the recommended SoLoPO procedure, chosen-only alignment, and standard DPO/SimPO/ORPO objectives remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use MuSiQue training data and the same LongBenchV1, RULER, LongBenchV2, Open LLM Leaderboard, and NIAH-Plus coverage. The new bound experiment uses existing QA tasks. Long-output applications remain proposed future work.

E2.justification: v3 adds both public-checkpoint and reimplemented LongPO comparisons to Table 4 for LongBenchV2 and Open LLM Leaderboard. Both appeared in Table 3 previously, but neither participated in v2's Table 4 comparison.

E3.justification: Appendix I.8 adds a controlled comparison of tight and loose alignment bounds on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, explicitly holding other training configurations fixed. Existing checkpoint selection, training budgets, prompts, decoding settings, and evaluation metrics are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix I.8 and Table 14 test whether alignment-bound tightness affects performance across DPO, SimPO, and ORPO. Existing chosen-only alignment, NIAH-Plus, coefficient sensitivity, training dynamics, and scalability analyses are retained, sometimes reordered.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations across five LongBenchV2 evaluation runs in Figure 8 and Table 4. New LongPO rows follow that existing practice; no new run-count policy, seed reporting, confidence intervals, or significance tests appear.

E6.justification: Table 4 newly reports LongPO public and reimplemented LongBenchV2 scores of 33.3±0.5 and 29.6±1.5. Table 14 adds loose-bound results, including SoLo-ORPO averages of 46.9 on LongBenchV1 and 62.6 on RULER; the existing standard-bound scores remain 49.5 and 65.1. Table 5 redisplays gains derived from previously reported NIAH-Plus scores.

T1.justification: Theorems 1–2 and their proofs are retained. Appendix I.8 adds bound definitions and a mathematical example about differing surrogate minimizers. That example incorrectly states x^4-x^2=x^2(x^2-2) and places its minimum at x=1; the actual minimizers of x^4-x^2 are ±1/sqrt(2).

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: decoupling long-context preference optimization, transferring short-context abilities, compatibility with mainstream PO algorithms, and improved efficiency and generalization. Added evidence and future-work examples do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 now acknowledges SoLo-DPO's slight short-context decline and discusses its trade-off with long-context performance. It adds a possible data-quality explanation for differences from LongPO. Appendices C, H.5, and I.8 expand discussion of long-output applicability, representation compression, and bound tightness.

D1.justification: v3 adds a first-page code/data link and a reproducibility statement describing source code, data examples, and usage instructions in supplementary materials. These are newly reported access provisions, not independently verified resources. Existing hardware, hyperparameters, and construction instructions remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds five cited works covering mathematical reasoning, long-chain reasoning, story generation, attention sinks, and Activation Beacon compression. These mainly support expanded motivation and future directions; the established positioning relative to LongPO, LOGO, and LongCE remains.

P1.justification: Most prose and the six-section main narrative are retained. v3 expands selected explanations, adds ethics, reproducibility, and LLM-use statements, and reorders limitations and appendix analyses. It also makes local terminology, notation, and affiliation edits.

P2.justification: Figure 1a corrects the SoLoPO component label from long-context to short-context preference optimization. v3 expands Table 4, adds the NIAH-Plus summary Table 5 and bound-analysis Table 14, and adjusts table highlighting and placement. Conference headers and typography change, while the experimental plots are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves assessability through the added LongPO comparisons, controlled bound experiment, clearer acknowledgment of the short-context trade-off, and reported code/data access. Figure 1a also corrects a misleading label. These benefits are partly offset by the algebra and minimizer errors in the new Appendix I.8 example; the principal method, proofs, and existing experimental evidence remain stable.
